newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-BHP rated long-term buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-BHP rated long-term buy.

text.p: Brokerage J.B. Were and Son has rated the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) a long-term buy, but warned that greater exposure to weak copper prices is likely to provide a major short-term drag on copper division earnings.

The brokerage forecast the battered copper division's net profit to drop to A$288 million in the year ending May 31, 1998, from A$438 million in the current 1996/97 year, then sliding further to A$211 million in 1998/99 and A$163 million in 1999/2000.

"Overall, BHP's long-term earnings growth is robust with major new projects and organic growth adding significantly to earnings out to and beyond 2000," it said in a research report compiled by BHP analyst Neil Goodwill.
"BHP Copper, however, which provided robust profits during 1994/95 and 1995/96 is set for a period of considerable weakeness as copper pricies continue to fall with increased supply."

The report forecast BHP's realised copper price to fall from 94 US cents per pound to 76 cents in 1999/2000, though it said prices were likely to "spike" in BHP's final quarter and give the division a chance to hedge and lock in the higher prices.
